article.headline: Inside a Crowd-Sourced Basket of Twenty-Nine AI-Era Micro-Caps
article.lede: Serenity, an X.com analyst who covers the AI hardware supply chain under the handle @aleabitoreddit, crowd-sourced a portfolio she calls the Followers Favorite Stock Parabolic Growth ETF: twenty-nine small and micro-cap names submitted by her followers as high-conviction bets on tenfold returns, each equally weighted at roughly 3.45 percent. She openly admitted to being unfamiliar with about a third of the tickers, treating collective follower conviction as a substitute for her own due diligence. The basket spans AI optical interconnects, directed-energy weapons, deep-sea minerals, and gene therapy — an index of retail investor obsessions in the spring of 2026.
article.body:
Serenity, whose feed concentrates on the AI hardware supply chain, built this basket by polling her followers for their highest-conviction name, then equal-weighting every submission at roughly 3.45 percent. The structure is deliberately flat: no position dominates, which means the portfolio is simultaneously a collective research exercise and a bet that a crowd aggregates private sector knowledge better than any single analyst. Her admission of not knowing a third of the holdings is not a disclaimer but part of the methodology — she is treating her follower network as distributed intelligence.

The backbone of the basket is an *AI optical interconnect* thesis running from laser fabrication to chip testing. Sivers Semiconductors (SIVE) makes *indium phosphide* distributed-feedback lasers — the light sources inside next-generation transceivers. Enablence Technologies (ENAFF) manufactures *planar lightwave circuit* couplers, the passive glass waveguides that route that light, and is formally partnered with Sivers on a *co-packaged optics* module for AI data centers. POET Technologies (POET) develops optical engines that let customers assemble high-density transceiver modules without owning a photonics fab. Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) sits at the finished-product end, manufacturing 800G and **1.6T** transceivers and guiding to more than $1 billion in 2026 revenue. Aehr Test Systems (AEHR) stress-tests *silicon photonics* chips at the wafer level before expensive packaging, while nLIGHT (LASR) supplies semiconductor and fiber lasers for both data-center fabrication equipment and directed-energy defense programs. The packaging angle is reinforced by two German names: LPKF Laser & Electronics (LPK.DE), whose proprietary *LIDE* process etches precision holes in thin glass for advanced chip substrates, and Plan Optik (P4O.DE), a micro-cap glass-wafer maker whose shares rallied more than 160 percent over twelve months as investors connected its product line to the *glass interposer* thesis. Photronics (PLAB), a *photomask* specialist serving virtually every major chipmaker, and Trio-Tech International (TRT), which provides burn-in test services for AI GPU silicon, complete the picks-and-shovels tier.

A second cluster groups defense modernization, edge AI, and critical materials. Electro Optic Systems (EOS.AX), an Australian maker of laser-weapon turrets and counter-drone systems, and Firefly Aerospace (FLY), a small-launch and lunar-delivery company with growing national-security revenue, sit alongside nLIGHT on the directed-energy side. Blaize Holdings (BZAI) designs edge AI processors for smart-city and defense applications; Gorilla Technology (GRRR) deploys AI video analytics while building GPU compute campuses in India and Southeast Asia; 2CRSi (AL2SI), a French GPU-server manufacturer, offers a more direct infrastructure exposure. Valens Semiconductor (VLN) makes high-speed chips for automotive camera links. The materials sub-basket includes EQ Resources (EQR.AX), one of the few non-Chinese tungsten producers, benefiting from surging *APT* prices and Western supply-security anxiety; ASP Isotopes (ASPI), which enriches isotopically pure Silicon-28 for quantum computing and recently signed its largest-ever supply contract; and TMC the metals company (TMC), which cleared a key US regulatory milestone in May 2026 in its bid to harvest *polymetallic nodules* from the Pacific floor for battery minerals.

Several names sit at a considerable remove from the AI and defense narrative. uniQure (QURE) is a *gene therapy* company running a Phase I/II program for Huntington's disease with a $586 million cash runway and no near-term commercial catalyst that would explain a tenfold move. Crossject (ALCJ), a French pre-revenue biotech, is developing a needle-free diazepam auto-injector funded partly by BARDA. Mitek Systems (MITK) is a profitable identity-verification *SaaS* business whose recent 18 percent year-on-year growth is sound but scarcely momentum-grade. Energous Corporation (WATT) is the one surprise story: a wireless-power company that was essentially a science project until a Fortune-10 retailer began deploying its technology across thousands of US stores, lifting quarterly revenue roughly tenfold year-on-year. EON Resources (EONR), a development-stage Permian Basin oil producer, has no obvious kinship with anything else in the list. HydroGraph Clean Power (HGRAF), a graphene manufacturer, and Aduro Clean Technologies (ADUR), a chemical-recycling startup, represent a cleantech tail with multiyear commercialization timelines. Vishay Precision Group (VPG), a precision-sensor specialist that recently announced robotics supply deals, is the most conventionally profitable name in the portfolio. Equal weighting means each outlier claims the same 3.45 percent slot as the photonics core — structurally, a gene-therapy binary event carries the same expected portfolio contribution as a transceiver ramp worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

The word “parabolic” is doing double duty. Several holdings have already posted violent upward moves: Sivers gained more than 1,200 percent year-to-date by early May 2026 before analysts raised questions about whether the rally had outrun fundamentals; nLIGHT hit an all-time high the same week; POET fell roughly 50 percent in a single week after disclosing an order cancellation from its largest customer. “Parabolic growth” here describes a trajectory already achieved as much as a target. Whether followers submitted these names at the inflection point between a genuine supply-chain ramp and a momentum cycle that has already priced in generous assumptions — and whether a crowd aggregates information or merely amplifies shared biases — is the productive tension this basket leaves unresolved.

concepts.definition: The technology and supply chain for transmitting data between chips and servers using pulses of light through fiber-optic cables rather than electrical signals. Optical links are faster, lower-latency, and more energy-efficient at the speeds required for large-scale AI model training and inference, driving a surge in demand for lasers, transceivers, and photonic packaging components.

A compound semiconductor made from indium and phosphorus that emits light efficiently at the infrared wavelengths used in fiber-optic communications. Preferred over silicon for making the laser diodes inside high-speed data-center transceivers because of its direct bandgap and high electron mobility; Sivers Semiconductors is one of the few independent western suppliers of InP laser dies.

An optical waveguide chip made by depositing silica glass layers on a silicon substrate. Routes and splits light beams passively — without electrical power — and is used in fiber splitters, optical couplers, and the passive sections of co-packaged optical modules. Enablence Technologies is a specialist manufacturer of PLC components.

An architecture that integrates optical transceiver hardware directly into the same physical package as a network switch or AI processor chip, eliminating lossy copper connections between them. A key frontier in data-center interconnect design as per-lane speeds scale to 1.6T and beyond; enables higher bandwidth density and lower power consumption per bit.

A manufacturing approach that builds optical components — waveguides, modulators, photodetectors — directly onto silicon wafers using standard semiconductor fabrication tools. Allows photonic circuits to be produced at chip-industry scale and cost, enabling affordable high-speed optical transceivers; Aehr Test Systems has developed burn-in equipment specifically for silicon photonics chips.

An optical module capable of transmitting 1.6 terabits of data per second, the current frontier for high-speed connections between AI accelerators and network switches inside hyperscale data centers. Successor to 800G modules; requires advanced indium phosphide lasers, silicon photonics integration, and co-packaged optics engineering to achieve the bandwidth density at acceptable power and cost.

Weapons that damage or destroy targets by delivering concentrated electromagnetic energy — typically a high-power laser beam or microwave pulse — rather than kinetic projectiles. Under rapid development globally for counter-drone and missile-defense applications, where speed-of-light delivery and low cost-per-shot are decisive advantages over conventional munitions.

A proprietary process developed by LPKF Laser & Electronics that uses focused ultrashort laser pulses to structurally modify thin glass, followed by a chemical etch that removes the altered material. Produces high-aspect-ratio holes and channels with precision unmatched by mechanical drilling, used to create the signal vias in advanced glass semiconductor packaging substrates.

A glass-based routing layer placed between a processor chip and its circuit board that carries high-speed electrical signals between chiplets. Glass offers lower signal loss, finer routing capability, and better thermal stability than organic or silicon alternatives, making it attractive for next-generation AI chip packaging; companies like Plan Optik and LPKF supply the precision glass and processing equipment this shift requires.

A high-precision quartz plate on which circuit patterns are etched in chrome or other opaque materials. Used as a stencil in semiconductor lithography to project those patterns onto silicon wafers via ultraviolet or extreme-UV light, printing each layer of a chip. Every new process node requires a fresh set of masks, making photomask manufacturers like Photronics structurally tied to chip industry investment cycles.

Stress-testing semiconductor chips under elevated voltage and temperature while they are still attached to the original silicon wafer, before individual die are cut out and packaged. Identifies latent manufacturing defects at the cheapest possible stage of production; particularly valuable for high-cost components such as AI GPUs and silicon photonics chips where a single bad part can cost hundreds of dollars.

The strategy of buying suppliers of tools and infrastructure to a booming industry rather than betting on which end-product companies will dominate. The analogy is to Gold Rush merchants who sold picks and shovels to every prospector: enabling companies capture value regardless of who wins the underlying race, with more predictable revenue and less binary risk than the product-level bets.

The intermediate chemical compound produced by refining tungsten ore, widely used as the benchmark price for global tungsten markets. APT prices surged roughly 300 percent from early 2025 as Western buyers sought to reduce dependence on Chinese tungsten supply amid geopolitical decoupling, directly benefiting non-Chinese producers like EQ Resources.

Potato-sized mineral concretions that form on the deep ocean floor over millions of years, containing commercially interesting concentrations of nickel, cobalt, copper, and manganese — all critical inputs for lithium-ion batteries and electronics. Mining them is technically feasible but faces significant environmental and international regulatory scrutiny; TMC the metals company holds exploration rights to a large nodule field in the Pacific.

A medical approach that treats disease by inserting, altering, or replacing genetic material inside a patient's cells, typically delivered by a modified virus known as a viral vector. Targets conditions caused by single-gene mutations; approved products exist for hemophilia (uniQure's HEMGENIX), but most programs for complex neurological diseases such as Huntington's remain in early clinical stages with highly binary outcomes.

The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, a US Department of Health and Human Services agency that funds development of medical countermeasures — vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics — against biological, chemical, radiological, and nuclear threats. BARDA contracts provide non-dilutive government funding but do not guarantee regulatory approval or commercial revenue for the funded products.

An early-stage human drug trial combining first-in-human safety testing (Phase I) with initial evidence of efficacy (Phase II) in a single study design. Common in rare-disease and neurological programs where eligible patient populations are too small to run sequential studies; positive Phase I/II data is encouraging but does not guarantee later-stage success or regulatory approval.

A portfolio construction method in which every holding receives the same percentage allocation regardless of the investor's conviction level, the holding's market capitalization, or its revenue size. Maximizes breadth and prevents concentration risk but treats a speculative pre-revenue biotech as structurally equivalent to a high-revenue transceiver manufacturer — a trade-off the Parabolic Growth ETF makes explicit.

article.fact_check: The self-description as “the most anticipated ETF of all time” is evidently tongue-in-cheek hyperbole. More substantively, the image OCR captures two tickers absent from the tweet body: GRRR (Gorilla Technology Group) fits the basket's AI theme credibly and is almost certainly a genuine holding omitted from the tweet text due to character limits. $THS is harder to square: if the OCR is accurate, it resolves to TreeHouse Foods (NYSE: THS), a private-label food company in the process of being taken private, which has no thematic connection to any other holding and is most likely a misread of another ticker. The OCR also renders one position as $FLYR rather than $FLY; $FLYR was a Norwegian low-cost airline that ceased operations in January 2023, while Firefly Aerospace (NASDAQ: FLY) is the correct match given the basket's space and defense theme. Finally, the prices listed in the tweet body are entry prices at time of composition; several holdings — including Sivers (SIVE) and nLIGHT (LASR) — have since moved far above those levels, while POET has traded sharply lower following an order cancellation event.

ticker_trt.name: Trio-Tech International
ticker_trt.blurb: Trio-Tech International provides burn-in and reliability testing equipment and services for the back-end semiconductor manufacturing process. Burn-in testing stresses chips under elevated voltage and temperature to flush out early failures before they reach end users — a quality step used for memory, logic, and increasingly AI GPU silicon. The company also operates test service centres in Southeast Asia. It is an indirect beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout through the semiconductor testing supply chain rather than a photonics company per se.
ticker_trt.recent: In March 2026, Trio-Tech secured a $5.3M order for burn-in boards for a next-generation AI GPU platform, signalling direct involvement in the GPU production supply chain. The stock gained approximately 421% over the trailing twelve months as of early May 2026, trading near $13.36. The gain reflects both the AI-hardware testing demand surge and the company's small-cap status, which magnifies price moves on modest volume increases.

ticker_hgraf.name: HydroGraph Clean Power Inc.
ticker_hgraf.exchange: OTCQB (U.S. OTC Markets); also listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange as HG
ticker_hgraf.blurb: HydroGraph Clean Power Inc. is a Vancouver, British Columbia–based specialty materials company founded in 2017 that produces fractal graphene using a patented 'explosion synthesis' process carried out in its proprietary Hyperion Reactor. Its flagship product, FGA-1, achieves 99.8% purity and is marketed to over 60 customers across 75+ commercial pipeline projects spanning medical devices, advanced composites, and industrial coatings. Each Hyperion Reactor measures roughly 6×6×18 feet and is rated for approximately 10 tons of graphene per year, positioning HydroGraph as an emerging supplier in an industry that has historically struggled to deliver graphene at industrial scale and economically viable pricing.
ticker_hgraf.recent: As of May 14, 2026, HGRAF shares were trading at approximately $5.05, down 2.70% on the session, with a 52-week range of $0.15–$8.37 and a market capitalization near $1.72 billion. The company commissioned two additional Hyperion Reactors in January and February 2026, and is relocating primary production from Manhattan, Kansas to a new 70,000 sq ft Austin, Texas facility targeting 350+ tons per year of graphene capacity across five reactors. No major earnings announcements or material contract disclosures were identified in the provided sources for the trailing 30-day window.

ticker_sive.name: Sivers Semiconductors AB (publ)
ticker_sive.blurb: Sivers designs and manufactures indium phosphide (InP) distributed feedback lasers and optical amplifiers used inside high-speed optical transceivers, automotive LiDAR systems and satellite communications terminals. Its photonics business is one of the few independent western sources of the laser dies that go into AI-data-centre optical links, alongside larger incumbents such as Coherent and Lumentum. A separate wireless unit supplies 5G millimetre-wave RF chips. The company has been preparing a spin-off and potential dual Nasdaq New York listing of its photonics subsidiary.
ticker_sive.recent: Shares ran from roughly SEK 4 at the start of 2026 to a close of SEK 55.95 in early May, a year-to-date gain of about 1,247%, on customer wins including a 1.6T linear-drive optical module collaboration with Jabil announced 15 April 2026 and a LiDAR ramp scheduled for Q4 2026 with up to $138m of cumulative lifetime revenue. 2025 net sales were SEK 304m (+25% YoY) but the after-tax loss was SEK 186m, prompting an April 2026 directed issue of 8.62m shares at SEK 14.50 raising about SEK 125m at roughly 2.5% dilution. Photonics experts and Swedish business media have publicly questioned whether the rally has run ahead of fundamentals.

ticker_enaff.blurb: Enablence Technologies Inc. is a Canadian photonics company focused on optical chips and integrated photonics components for datacom, telecom, artificial intelligence infrastructure, automotive sensing, and LiDAR applications. The company develops planar lightwave circuit (PLC) technology used to route and split optical signals in fiber-optic networks. Its products target the intersection of growing AI compute interconnect demand and next-generation optical networking. Enablence trades in the U.S. over-the-counter market under the ticker ENAFF.

ticker_poet.name: POET Technologies Inc.
ticker_poet.blurb: POET Technologies develops optical engines — compact co-packaged modules that integrate lasers and photonic integrated circuits — targeting 400G, 800G, and 1.6T AI data-centre interconnect applications. Its POET Infinity platform is designed to allow customers to assemble high-density optical transceiver modules without owning their own photonics fabrication. The company raised approximately $375M in equity in Q4 2025 and carries roughly $430M in cash.
ticker_poet.recent: POET experienced one of the more dramatic volatility events in the photonics sector during April 2026. Shares rallied roughly 108% on reports its technology was being integrated into Marvell Technology's AI hardware stack via Celestial AI (which Marvell had acquired). On April 27, 2026, POET disclosed it had received notice of order cancellation from Marvell on April 23, with Marvell citing a confidentiality violation; shares fell approximately 50% in a single week. POET countered with a separate $5M production order for Infinity engines targeting 30,000+ units in 2026, and maintained partnerships with LITEON and Lessengers for 1.6T modules. The episode became a widely-cited example of single-customer concentration risk in small-cap photonics. @Ren_aramb's post singles out POET as the notable exception in an otherwise rising sector.

ticker_aaoi.name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
ticker_aaoi.blurb: Applied Optoelectronics is a Texas-based maker of optical components and transceivers, historically known for serving cable-television networks and a handful of hyperscale customers in cycles of feast and famine. The AI build-out has dragged it firmly into the data-centre supply chain, where it now competes for 400G, 800G, and 1.6T transceiver volumes against Lumentum, Coherent, Innolight, and Eoptolink.
ticker_aaoi.recent: Management is guiding to full-year 2026 revenue exceeding $1 billion, more than double 2025's roughly $456 million, on the back of 800G ramps and a single 1.6T order disclosed at over $200 million. The company aims to scale from roughly 90,000 800G units per month at end-2025 toward 500,000 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026. The stock hit an all-time high near $192 in early May 2026, having traded as low as $12.56 within the last 52 weeks.

ticker_aehr.name: Aehr Test Systems
ticker_aehr.blurb: Aehr Test Systems designs and manufactures wafer-level burn-in and test equipment for semiconductors, with a specialisation in silicon carbide (SiC) power devices, gallium nitride (GaN), and — increasingly — silicon photonics chips. Its flagship FOX-XP system stress-tests devices while still on the wafer, before costly packaging, identifying failures at the cheapest possible point in manufacturing. Aehr claims to be the first company to ship a multi-wafer burn-in solution for silicon photonics transceivers. The company is headquartered in Fremont, California.
ticker_aehr.recent: In March 2026, Aehr won a new silicon photonics customer for its high-power FOX-XP wafer-level burn-in system targeting hyperscale data-centre optical interconnects. Quarterly bookings reached $37.2 million in the quarter ending February 2026 — a book-to-bill ratio exceeding 3.5x — with the company guiding full-year FY2026 revenue toward the high end of its $45–$50 million range. Revenue in the same quarter was $10.3 million, down from $18.3 million a year earlier, reflecting a timing gap between order intake and shipment schedules weighted toward the second half of 2026.

ticker_lasr.name: nLIGHT, Inc.
ticker_lasr.blurb: nLIGHT, Inc. is a Vancouver, Washington-based manufacturer of high-power semiconductor and fiber lasers used in industrial, microfabrication, and aerospace/defense applications. The company designs its own laser chips and integrates them into complete laser systems, giving it vertical integration advantages over competitors. nLIGHT serves both commercial markets (sheet-metal cutting, welding) and growing defense markets (directed-energy weapons, beam-control systems). Its defense segment has become an increasingly important revenue driver as U.S. military demand for high-energy laser systems expands.
ticker_lasr.recent: nLIGHT reported a Q1 2026 earnings beat driven by surging defense demand and the launch of a new laser platform, sending shares sharply higher. Management issued upbeat guidance, citing defense-driven momentum as a key catalyst for the near-term outlook. The stock jumped following the print as investors reacted positively to both the outperformance and the forward visibility provided by growing government contracts.

ticker_plab.description: Photronics is one of the world's leading manufacturers of photomasks — the high-precision glass reticles used in semiconductor and flat panel display lithography to transfer circuit patterns onto silicon wafers. Operating eleven facilities across Asia, Europe, and North America, it serves virtually every major chipmaker. The business is structurally tied to node migration: each new process generation requires new mask sets. Q1 FY2026 revenue was $225 million (+6% YoY), with $588 million in cash, zero meaningful debt, and a $330 million capex plan to expand U.S. and Korean capacity.

ticker_eos-ax.name: Electro Optic Systems Holdings Limited
ticker_eos-ax.blurb: Electro Optic Systems Holdings Limited is an Australian defence and space technology company specialising in electro-optic systems, remote weapon stations, and space domain awareness. Its defence segment produces automated and remotely operated weapons systems used by military forces, while its space segment develops laser-based systems for tracking and communicating with satellites and space debris. The company operates primarily in Australia, the Middle East, and other international defence markets. With a market capitalisation of approximately A$1.63 billion, EOS has grown into one of Australia's more prominent listed defence contractors.

On May 14, 2026, the company filed a 'Becoming a substantial holder' announcement with the ASX, indicating a new or increased major shareholding position. A 'Ceasing to be a substantial holder' notice was also filed on May 7, 2026, suggesting active institutional shareholder movement around the stock.

ticker_fly.name: Firefly Aerospace Inc.
ticker_fly.blurb: Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company providing integrated launch and space services for national security, government, and commercial customers. Its launch portfolio includes Alpha, a small responsive launch vehicle, and Eclipse, a medium-lift rocket under development.
